desc:
The string s consists only of the characters 0 and 1. Find the shortest substring (contiguous) that contains exactly k characters equal to 1 and return its length. Return -1 if s has fewer than k ones.

s = "1001010", k = 2
substring "101" (indices 3..5) has two ones
result = 3
constraints: s contains only the characters 0 and 1
hints: A substring with exactly k ones that is as short as possible never begins or ends with a 0. Why not?
So the substring starts at one particular 1 and ends at another 1 exactly k - 1 ones later.
Collect the positions of all ones in a list pos. The candidate lengths are pos[i + k - 1] - pos[i] + 1. Equivalently, slide a window that holds k ones and trim its zero ends.
editorial: If a substring with exactly k ones starts or ends with a zero, dropping that zero keeps the number of ones and shortens the substring. So an optimal substring starts at a 1 and ends at a 1, and it contains the ones numbered i through i + k - 1 in order.

Record the index of every 1. For each i with i + k - 1 inside the list, the length is pos[i + k - 1] - pos[i] + 1; the answer is the minimum, or -1 when there are fewer than k ones. This is a fixed-size window over the list of ones, taking O(n) time and O(n) space (a two-pointer version with a counter needs only O(1) extra space).
